messages.subject: Joint zero inflation models using R-INLA
parts:
If we use Zero Inflated Poisson and Hurdle model which gives both zero inflation model results and count model results, 

Then in R-INLA we can use zeroinflatedpoisson1 and zeroinflatedpoisson0 respectively.

My question is; 

when we create Y matrix for joint models;

does this code gives correct outputs?

n = no. of oberv

Zero Inflated Poisson model Poisson Hurdle model
n.y = n.z = n n.y = n.z = n
z <- rep(0,n) count[count == 0] <- NA
z[which(count > 0 | count == 0)]<-1
y = count z <- rep(0,n)
z[which(count > 0)]<-1
y = count
tmp =rep(NA, 4 * n) tmp =rep(NA, 4 * n)
Y = matrix(tmp, ncol = 2) Y = matrix(tmp, ncol = 2)
Y[1:n, 1] = z Y[1:n, 1] = z
Y[(n + 1):(2*n), 2] = y Y[(n + 1):(2*n), 2] = y
mu.z = rep(1:0, c(n, n)) mu.z = rep(1:0, c(n, n))
mu.y = rep(0:1, c(n, n)) mu.y = rep(0:1, c(n, n))
data = list(Y = Y, mu.z = mu.z, mu.y = mu.y) data = list(Y = Y, mu.z = mu.z, mu.y = mu.y)
fit <- inla(Y ~ 0 + mu.z + mu.y,  fit <- inla(Y ~ 0 + mu.z + mu.y, 
             data = data, family = c("binomial", "zeroinflatednbinomial1"),               data = data, family = c("binomial", "zeroinflatednbinomial0"), 
             control.family = list(list(link = "logit"), list(link = "log")),              control.family = list(list(link = "logit"), list(link = "log")),
             control.compute = list(dic = TRUE,cpo = TRUE, po = TRUE))               control.compute = list(dic = TRUE,cpo = TRUE, po = TRUE)) 
summary(fit) summary(fit)

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Joint zero inflation models using R-INLA
parts:
AFAIK, zeroinflatednbinomial1 requires a single vector response containing both 0 and non zero counts. It has a single (constant) parameter estimating the zero inflation.

zeroinflatednbinomial0 can work in the same way as zeroinflatednbinomial0. However, here you can split it in a two vector matrix. One vector containing 0 (non-zero count) and 1 (zero count) and another vector containing the counts (non-zero counts) and NA (zero counts). Then you can use binomial to model the non-zero vs zero and zeroinflatednbinomial0 to model the zero-truncated counts by setting the prior of the zero inflation so that the hurdle model has a (near) 0 probability of zero's (the true probability of zero is modelled by the binomial).
